newsitem.title: UK: Steel Burrill profits down, sees hostile 1997.
newsitem.headline: Steel Burrill profits down, sees hostile 1997.

text.p: Insurance broker Steel Burrill Jones on Thursday reported a 61 percent fall in 1996 pre-tax profits to 2.21 million stg ($3.5 million) and said that conditions would remain difficult in the current year.

"The environment will remain hostile during 1997 with insurance rates declining in most markets. This will adversely affect our London market business but recruitment and consequent additional income should mitigate this," chairman Clive Richards said.
Brokerage and fees overall fell eight percent to 39.94 million stg from 43.19 million in 1995, SBJ said in a statement.
London market brokerage and fees slumped 19 percent to 18.80 million stg from 23.27 million, but UK retail brokerage and fees rose seven percent to 21.11 million from 19.64 million.
"Our retail businesses should show further good growth. We are working hard in 1997 to lay the foundations for a resumption in overall growth at the earliest opportunity," Richards said.

However, SBJ said London market operations were hit by the full year effect of the contraction of the group's non-marine reinsurance activities in 1995 and the harsh trading conditions which prevailed throughout the period.
The broker reduced expenses to 41.87 million stg last year from 42.82 million stg.
SBJ said its future strategy was based on remaining independent, increasing its fee-based business and expanding its revenue through recruitment.
It said its retail activities continued to grow and now represented over 60 percent of turnover.
"The majority of this is fee based and allows the group to earn a return directly related to the professionals services it provides, reducing dependence on the vagaries of insurance pricing."
Recent broker consolidation in London and internationally would benefit the company, SBJ said.
"We are actively cultivating the many opportunities arising from this consolidation both in terms of recruitment of new insurance professionals and additions to our client list."
However, SBJ said that, like other brokers, the continuing soft market for most lines of insurance continued to work against it.
-- Reuters Insurance News 44 171 542 2769 ($ = 0.624 British Pounds Sterling)
